Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:11:## Problem
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:13:Long-running agent conversations with many tool calls can suffer from **quadratic performance degradation**:
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:18:- **Configuration changes**: Mid-conversation changes (sandbox, tools, working directory) can break cache efficiency
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:22:## Solution
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:24:Maintain prompt cache efficiency through **exact prefix preservation** - always append new messages rather than modifying existing ones, and carefully order messages to maximize cache hits.
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:26:**Core insight**: Prompt caches only work on **exact prefix matches**. If the first N tokens of a request match a previous request, the cached computation can be reused.
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:28:**Mechanism**: Caching operates at the token level, not message level. The cache checks token-by-token for prefix matches, independent of message boundaries.
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:32:1. **Static content first** (beginning of prompt - cached across all requests):
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:38:2. **Variable content last** (end of prompt - changes per request):
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:57:This preserves the exact prefix of all previous messages, maintaining cache hits.
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:59:**What breaks cache hits:**
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:69:- **Anthropic**: Explicit cache-control headers, TTL-based invalidation (up to 5 minutes), 90% discount on cached tokens
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:73:Avoid `previous_response_id` to support Zero Data Retention. Instead, rely on prompt caching for linear performance:
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:78:- Linear sampling cost (due to prompt caching)
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:85:## Example
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:137:## How to use it
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:152:| Tool list | Change mid-conversation | Avoid if possible; breaks cache |
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:156:MCP servers can emit `notifications/tools/list_changed` to indicate tool list changes. **Avoid honoring this mid-conversation** as it breaks cache hits. Instead:
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:158:- Or accept the cache miss as necessary trade-off
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:160:**Implementation sketch:**
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:166:  // Static prefix (cached)
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:196:## Trade-offs
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:208:- **Quadratic network traffic**: JSON payload size still grows quadratically (only sampling is cached)
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:212:- **MCP server limitations**: Dynamic tool changes can cause cache misses

--- Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/README.md
1:# Awesome Agentic Patterns
2:
3:![Awesome Agentic Patterns](/agentic-patterns.jpeg)
4:
5:A curated catalogue of **agentic AI patterns** — real‑world tricks, workflows, and mini‑architectures that help autonomous or semi‑autonomous AI agents get useful work done in production.
6:
7:> **Why?**
8:> Tutorials show toy demos. Real products hide the messy bits. This list surfaces the repeatable patterns that bridge the gap so we can all ship smarter, faster agents.
9:
10:---
11:
12:## What counts as a pattern?
13:
14:* **Repeatable** – more than one team is using it.
15:* **Agent‑centric** – improves how an AI agent senses, reasons, or acts.
16:* **Traceable** – backed by a public reference: blog post, talk, repo, or paper.
17:
18:If your link ticks those boxes, it belongs here.
19:
20:---
21:
22:## 🌐 Explore the Website
23:
24:**Visit:** [https://agentic-patterns.com](https://agentic-patterns.com)
25:
26:The website offers powerful discovery tools beyond this README:
27:
28:- **Pattern Explorer**: Browse, filter, and search all patterns by category, status, complexity, and more
29:- **Compare Tool**: Side-by-side comparison of multiple patterns with shared attributes
30:- **Decision Explorer**: Interactive guide to find the right pattern for your use case
31:- **Graph Visualization**: Visual map of pattern relationships and connections
32:- **Pattern Packs**: Curated collections of patterns for common agent architectures
33:- **Developer Guides**: In-depth documentation on pattern selection and usage
34:- **Dark Mode**: Full theme support for comfortable reading in any environment
35:
36:Built with [Astro](https://astro.build), deployed on [Vercel](https://vercel.com), source code in [`apps/web/`](./apps/web/).

--- Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md
1:---
2:title: "Prompt Caching via Exact Prefix Preservation"
3:status: emerging
4:authors: ["Nikola Balic (@nibzard)"]
5:based_on: ["Michael Bolin (OpenAI Codex)"]
6:category: "Context & Memory"
7:source: "https://openai.com/index/unrolling-the-codex-agent-loop/"
8:tags: [prompt-caching, exact-prefix, performance, stateless, zero-data-retention, message-ordering, optimization]
9:---
10:
11:## Problem
12:
13:Long-running agent conversations with many tool calls can suffer from **quadratic performance degradation**:
14:
15:- **Growing JSON payloads**: Each iteration sends the entire conversation history to the API
16:- **Expensive re-computation**: Without caching, the model re-processes the same static content repeatedly
17:- **ZDR constraints**: Zero Data Retention (ZDR) policies prevent server-side state, ruling out `previous_response_id` optimization
18:- **Configuration changes**: Mid-conversation changes (sandbox, tools, working directory) can break cache efficiency
19:
20:As conversations grow, inference costs and latency increase quadratically without proper caching strategies.
21:
22:## Solution
23:
24:Maintain prompt cache efficiency through **exact prefix preservation** - always append new messages rather than modifying existing ones, and carefully order messages to maximize cache hits.
25:
26:**Core insight**: Prompt caches only work on **exact prefix matches**. If the first N tokens of a request match a previous request, the cached computation can be reused.
27:
28:**Mechanism**: Caching operates at the token level, not message level. The cache checks token-by-token for prefix matches, independent of message boundaries.
29:
30:**Message ordering strategy:**
31:
32:1. **Static content first** (beginning of prompt - cached across all requests):
33:   - System message (if server-controlled)
34:   - Tool definitions (must be in consistent order)
35:   - Developer instructions
36:   - User/project instructions
37:
38:2. **Variable content last** (end of prompt - changes per request):
39:   - User message
40:   - Assistant messages
41:   - Tool call results (appended iteratively)
42:
43:**Configuration change via insertion:**
44:
45:When configuration changes mid-conversation, **insert a new message** rather than modifying an existing one:
46:
47:```
48:[Static prefix...]
49:<sandbox_config_v1>     // Original config message
50:[Conversation...]
51:
52:<sandbox changed>
53:<sandbox_config_v2>     // NEW message inserted
54:[Conversation continues...]
55:```
56:
57:This preserves the exact prefix of all previous messages, maintaining cache hits.
58:
59:**What breaks cache hits:**
60:
61:- Changing the list of available tools (position-sensitive)
62:- Reordering messages
63:- Modifying existing message content
64:- Changing the model (affects server-side system message)
65:
66:**Provider variations:**
67:
68:- **OpenAI**: Automatic caching on exact prefix matches
69:- **Anthropic**: Explicit cache-control headers, TTL-based invalidation (up to 5 minutes), 90% discount on cached tokens
70:
73:Avoid `previous_response_id` to support Zero Data Retention. Instead, rely on prompt caching for linear performance:
78:- Linear sampling cost (due to prompt caching)
96:    subgraph "Request 2 - Cache Hit!"
105:    subgraph "Request 3 - Cache Hit!"
135:**Green = Cached** (exact prefix match) | **Pink = Recomputed** (new tokens)
139:**Prompt construction checklist:**
152:| Tool list | Change mid-conversation | Avoid if possible; breaks cache |
156:MCP servers can emit `notifications/tools/list_changed` to indicate tool list changes. **Avoid honoring this mid-conversation** as it breaks cache hits. Instead:
158:- Or accept the cache miss as necessary trade-off
160:**Implementation sketch:**
163:function buildPrompt(state: ConversationState): Prompt {
164:  const items: PromptItem[] = [];
166:  // Static prefix (cached)
200:- **Linear sampling cost**: Prompt caching makes repeated inference linear rather than quadratic
204:- **Production-validated savings**: 43% cost reduction demonstrated at scale (HyperAgent, 9.4B tokens/month)
208:- **Quadratic network traffic**: JSON payload size still grows quadratically (only sampling is cached)
209:- **Cache fragility**: Mid-conversation changes (tools, model) break prefix matching
212:- **MCP server limitations**: Dynamic tool changes can cause cache misses

64:## 💡 Why this exists
65:
66:You shouldn't have to rebuild the same RAG pipeline, agent loop, or MCP integration from scratch every time you start a new LLM project.
67:
68:**Awesome LLM Apps is a cookbook of ready-to-run templates** - starter code you can fork, customize, and ship as a production LLM app. Every template here is self-contained with full source code, not collected from elsewhere.
69:
70:- 🛠️ **Hand-built, not curated** - every template is original work, tested end-to-end before it ships.
71:- 🧪 **Runs in 3 commands** - no broken `requirements.txt`, no "figure it out yourself" scaffolding.
72:- 🧠 **Covers the modern AI stack** - AI Agents, Multi-agent Teams, MCP Agents, Voice AI Agents, RAG, Agent Skills, Fine-tuning.
73:- 🌐 **Provider-agnostic** - switch between Claude, Gemini, GPT, Llama, Qwen, xAI and others with a config change.
74:- 📚 **Step-by-step tutorials** - every featured template has a free walkthrough on [Unwind AI](https://www.theunwindai.com).
75:- 💸 **Apache-2.0** - fork it, ship it, sell it. No paywall, no signup, no telemetry.
76:
77:> ⭐ **If this saves you time, [star the repo](https://github.com/Shubhamsaboo/awesome-llm-apps/stargazers) - that's how the next developer discovers it.**
78:

Z:/repos/deps/gitnexus/README.md:328:**How it works:** Each `gitnexus analyze` stores the index in `.gitnexus/` inside the repo (portable, gitignored) and registers a pointer in `~/.gitnexus/registry.json`. When an AI agent starts, the MCP server reads the registry and can serve any indexed repo. LadybugDB connections are opened lazily on first query and evicted after 5 minutes of inactivity (max 5 concurrent). If only one repo is indexed, the `repo` parameter is optional on all tools — agents don't need to change anything.

31:Indexes any codebase into a knowledge graph — every dependency, call chain, cluster, and execution flow — then exposes it through smart tools so AI agents never miss code.
32:

34:
35:
36:https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/172685ba-8e54-4ea7-9ad1-e31a3398da72

38:
39:
40:> *Like DeepWiki, but deeper.* DeepWiki helps you *understand* code. GitNexus lets you *analyze* it — because a knowledge graph tracks every relationship, not just descriptions.
41:
42:**TL;DR:** The **Web UI** is a quick way to chat with any repo. The **CLI + MCP** is how you make your AI agent actually reliable — it gives Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and friends a deep architectural view of your codebase so they stop missing dependencies, breaking call chains, and shipping blind edits. Even smaller models get full architectural clarity, making it compete with Goliath models.

51:## Two Ways to Use GitNexus
52:
53:|                   | **CLI + MCP**                                            | **Web UI**                                             |
54:| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
55:| **What**    | Index repos locally, connect AI agents via MCP                 | Visual graph explorer + AI chat in browser                   |
56:| **For**     | Daily development with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Windsurf, OpenCode | Quick exploration, demos, one-off analysis                   |
57:| **Scale**   | Full repos, any size                                           | Limited by browser memory (~5k files), or unlimited via backend mode |
58:| **Install** | `npm install -g gitnexus`                                    | No install — [gitnexus.vercel.app](https://gitnexus.vercel.app) |
59:| **Storage** | LadybugDB native (fast, persistent)                               | LadybugDB WASM (in-memory, per session)                         |
60:| **Parsing** | Tree-sitter native bindings                                    | Tree-sitter WASM                                             |
61:| **Privacy** | Everything local, no network                                   | Everything in-browser, no server                             |
62:
63:> **Bridge mode:** `gitnexus serve` connects the two — the web UI auto-detects the local server and can browse all your CLI-indexed repos without re-uploading or re-indexing.

97:## CLI + MCP (recommended)
99:The CLI indexes your repository and runs an MCP server that gives AI agents deep codebase awareness.
105:npx gitnexus analyze
108:That's it. This indexes the codebase, installs agent skills, registers Claude Code hooks, and creates `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` context files — all in one command.
110:To configure MCP for your editor, run `npx gitnexus setup` once — or set it up manually below.
112:> **Faster install (no C++ toolchain needed):** set `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS=1` before `npm install -g gitnexus` to skip the native `tree-sitter-dart` and `tree-sitter-proto` builds. Dart/Proto files won't be parsed, but install completes in seconds without `python3`/`make`/`g++`. Strict `=1` only — any other value falls through to the rebuild.
114:### MCP Setup
116:`gitnexus setup` auto-detects your editors and writes the correct global MCP config. You only need to run it once.
120:| Editor                | MCP | Skills | Hooks (auto-augment) | Support        |
122:| **Claude Code** | Yes | Yes    | Yes (PreToolUse + PostToolUse) | **Full** |
123:| **Cursor**      | Yes | Yes    | —                   | MCP + Skills   |
124:| **Codex**       | Yes | Yes    | —                   | MCP + Skills   |
125:| **Windsurf**    | Yes | —     | —                   | MCP            |
126:| **OpenCode**    | Yes | Yes    | —                   | MCP + Skills   |
128:> **Claude Code** gets the deepest integration: MCP tools + agent skills + PreToolUse hooks that enrich searches with graph context + PostToolUse hooks that detect a stale index after commits and prompt the agent to reindex.
136:| [pi-gitnexus](https://github.com/tintinweb/pi-gitnexus) | [@tintinweb](https://github.com/tintinweb) | GitNexus plugin for [pi](https://pi.dev) — `pi install npm:pi-gitnexus` |
137:| [gitnexus-stable-ops](https://github.com/ShunsukeHayashi/gitnexus-stable-ops) | [@ShunsukeHayashi](https://github.com/ShunsukeHayashi) | Stable ops & deployment workflows (Miyabi ecosystem) |
139:> Have a project built on GitNexus? Open a PR to add it here!
143:> **Recommended for fastest startup:** install gitnexus globally (`npm i -g gitnexus`) and run `gitnexus setup` — this writes an absolute-path MCP config that bypasses `npx` entirely. The pinned-`npx` snippets below are a quickstart fallback; on a cold cache the `npx` install can exceed Claude Code's `MCP_TIMEOUT` default (~30s).
145:**Claude Code** (full support — MCP + skills + hooks):
149:claude mcp add gitnexus -- npx -y gitnexus@latest mcp
152:claude mcp add gitnexus -- cmd /c npx -y gitnexus@latest mcp
155:**Codex** (full support — MCP + skills):
158:codex mcp add gitnexus -- npx -y gitnexus@latest mcp

195:### CLI Commands
198:gitnexus setup                   # Configure MCP for your editors (one-time)
199:gitnexus analyze [path]          # Index a repository (or update stale index)
200:gitnexus analyze --force         # Force full re-index
201:gitnexus analyze --skills        # Generate repo-specific skill files from detected communities
202:gitnexus analyze --skip-embeddings  # Skip embedding generation (faster)
203:gitnexus analyze --skip-agents-md  # Preserve custom AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md gitnexus section edits
204:gitnexus analyze --skip-git        # Index folders that are not Git repositories
205:gitnexus analyze --embeddings    # Enable embedding generation (slower, better search)
206:gitnexus analyze --verbose       # Log skipped files when parsers are unavailable
207:gitnexus analyze --worker-timeout 60  # Increase worker idle timeout for slow parses
208:gitnexus mcp                     # Start MCP server (stdio) — serves all indexed repos
209:gitnexus serve                   # Start local HTTP server (multi-repo) for web UI connection
210:gitnexus list                    # List all indexed repositories
211:gitnexus status                  # Show index status for current repo
212:gitnexus clean                   # Delete index for current repo
213:gitnexus clean --all --force     # Delete all indexes
214:gitnexus wiki [path]             # Generate repository wiki from knowledge graph
215:gitnexus wiki --model <model>    # Wiki with custom LLM model (default: gpt-4o-mini)
216:gitnexus wiki --base-url <url>   # Wiki with custom LLM API base URL
219:gitnexus group create <name>                                   # Create a repository group
220:gitnexus group add <group> <groupPath> <registryName>          # Add a repo to a group. <groupPath> is a hierarchy path (e.g. hr/hiring/backend); <registryName> is the repo's name from the registry (see `gitnexus list`)
221:gitnexus group remove <group> <groupPath>                      # Remove a repo from a group by its hierarchy path
222:gitnexus group list [name]                                     # List groups, or show one group's config
223:gitnexus group sync <name>                                     # Extract contracts and match across repos/services
224:gitnexus group contracts <name>  # Inspect extracted contracts and cross-links
225:gitnexus group query <name> <q>  # Search execution flows across all repos in a group
226:gitnexus group status <name>     # Check staleness of repos in a group
229:If `analyze` reports a worker parse timeout on a large or unusual repository, it keeps running and falls back safely. To give slow worker jobs more time, use `gitnexus analyze --worker-timeout 60` or set `GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=60000`. For very large files, `GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_MAX_BYTES` controls the worker job byte budget.
233:**16 tools** exposed via MCP (11 per-repo + 5 group):
256:| `gitnexus://repos`                      | List all indexed repositories (read this first)      |
257:| `gitnexus://repo/{name}/context`        | Codebase stats, staleness check, and available tools |
258:| `gitnexus://repo/{name}/clusters`       | All functional clusters with cohesion scores         |
259:| `gitnexus://repo/{name}/cluster/{name}` | Cluster members and details                          |
260:| `gitnexus://repo/{name}/processes`      | All execution flows                                  |
261:| `gitnexus://repo/{name}/process/{name}` | Full process trace with steps                        |
262:| `gitnexus://repo/{name}/schema`         | Graph schema for Cypher queries                      |
264:**2 MCP prompts** for guided workflows:
271:**4 agent skills** installed to `.claude/skills/` automatically:
280:When you run `gitnexus analyze --skills`, GitNexus detects the functional areas of your codebase (via Leiden community detection) and generates a `SKILL.md` file for each one under `.claude/skills/generated/`. Each skill describes a module's key files, entry points, execution flows, and cross-area connections — so your AI agent gets targeted context for the exact area of code you're working in. Skills are regenerated on each `--skills` run to stay current with the codebase.
284:## Multi-Repo MCP Architecture
286:GitNexus uses a **global registry** so one MCP server can serve multiple indexed repos. No per-project MCP config needed — set it up once and it works everywhere.
290:    subgraph CLI [CLI Commands]
291:        Setup["gitnexus setup"]
292:        Analyze["gitnexus analyze"]
293:        Clean["gitnexus clean"]
294:        List["gitnexus list"]
297:    subgraph Registry ["~/.gitnexus/"]
302:        RepoA[".gitnexus/ in repo A"]
303:        RepoB[".gitnexus/ in repo B"]
306:    subgraph MCP [MCP Server]
314:    Setup -->|"writes global MCP config"| CursorConfig["~/.cursor/mcp.json"]
328:**How it works:** Each `gitnexus analyze` stores the index in `.gitnexus/` inside the repo (portable, gitignored) and registers a pointer in `~/.gitnexus/registry.json`. When an AI agent starts, the MCP server reads the registry and can serve any indexed repo. LadybugDB connections are opened lazily on first query and evicted after 5 minutes of inactivity (max 5 concurrent). If only one repo is indexed, the `repo` parameter is optional on all tools — agents don't need to change anything.
334:A client-side graph explorer and AI chat — your code never leaves your machine.
336:**Try it now:** [gitnexus.vercel.app](https://gitnexus.vercel.app) — run `npx gitnexus@latest serve` locally and the page auto-connects to your local backend.

--- Z:/repos/deps/addyosmani-agent-skills/README.md
1:# Agent Skills
2:
3:**Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.**
4:
5:Skills encode the workflows, quality gates, and best practices that senior engineers use when building software. These ones are packaged so AI agents follow them consistently across every phase of development.
6:
7:```
8:  DEFINE          PLAN           BUILD          VERIFY         REVIEW          SHIP
9: ┌──────┐      ┌──────┐      ┌──────┐      ┌──────┐      ┌──────┐      ┌──────┐
10: │ Idea │ ───▶ │ Spec │ ───▶ │ Code │ ───▶ │ Test │ ───▶ │  QA  │ ───▶ │  Go  │
11: │Refine│      │  PRD │      │ Impl │      │Debug │      │ Gate │      │ Live │
12: └──────┘      └──────┘      └──────┘      └──────┘      └──────┘      └──────┘
13:  /spec          /plan          /build        /test         /review       /ship
14:```
15:
16:---
17:
18:## Commands
19:
20:7 slash commands that map to the development lifecycle. Each one activates the right skills automatically.
21:
22:| What you're doing | Command | Key principle |
23:|-------------------|---------|---------------|
24:| Define what to build | `/spec` | Spec before code |
25:| Plan how to build it | `/plan` | Small, atomic tasks |
26:| Build incrementally | `/build` | One slice at a time |
27:| Prove it works | `/test` | Tests are proof |
28:| Review before merge | `/review` | Improve code health |
29:| Simplify the code | `/code-simplify` | Clarity over cleverness |
30:| Ship to production | `/ship` | Faster is safer |
31:
32:Skills also activate automatically based on what you're doing — designing an API triggers `api-and-interface-design`, building UI triggers `frontend-ui-engineering`, and so on.
33:
34:---

128:## All 21 Skills
130:The commands above are entry points. The pack includes 21 skills total — each a structured workflow with steps, verification gates, and anti-rationalization tables. You can also reference any skill directly.
132:### Meta - Discover which skill applies
134:| Skill | What It Does | Use When |
136:| [using-agent-skills](skills/using-agent-skills/SKILL.md) | Maps incoming work to the right skill workflow and defines shared operating rules | Starting a session or deciding which skill applies |
138:### Define - Clarify what to build
140:| Skill | What It Does | Use When |
142:| [idea-refine](skills/idea-refine/SKILL.md) | Structured divergent/convergent thinking to turn vague ideas into concrete proposals | You have a rough concept that needs exploration |
143:| [spec-driven-development](skills/spec-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Write a PRD covering objectives, commands, structure, code style, testing, and boundaries before any code | Starting a new project, feature, or significant change |
145:### Plan - Break it down
147:| Skill | What It Does | Use When |
149:| [planning-and-task-breakdown](skills/planning-and-task-breakdown/SKILL.md) | Decompose specs into small, verifiable tasks with acceptance criteria and dependency ordering | You have a spec and need implementable units |
151:### Build - Write the code
153:| Skill | What It Does | Use When |
155:| [incremental-implementation](skills/incremental-implementation/SKILL.md) | Thin vertical slices - implement, test, verify, commit. Feature flags, safe defaults, rollback-friendly changes | Any change touching more than one file |
156:| [test-driven-development](skills/test-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Red-Green-Refactor, test pyramid (80/15/5), test sizes, DAMP over DRY, Beyonce Rule, browser testing | Implementing logic, fixing bugs, or changing behavior |
157:| [context-engineering](skills/context-engineering/SKILL.md) | Feed agents the right information at the right time - rules files, context packing, MCP integrations | Starting a session, switching tasks, or when output quality drops |
158:| [source-driven-development](skills/source-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Ground every framework decision in official documentation - verify, cite sources, flag what's unverified | You want authoritative, source-cited code for any framework or library |
159:| [doubt-driven-development](skills/doubt-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Adversarial fresh-context review of every non-trivial decision in-flight - CLAIM → EXTRACT → DOUBT → RECONCILE → STOP, with optional user-authorized cross-model escalation | Stakes are high (production, security, irreversible), working in unfamiliar code, or a confident output is cheaper to verify now than to debug later |
160:| [frontend-ui-engineering](skills/frontend-ui-engineering/SKILL.md) | Component architecture, design systems, state management, responsive design, WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility | Building or modifying user-facing interfaces |
161:| [api-and-interface-design](skills/api-and-interface-design/SKILL.md) | Contract-first design, Hyrum's Law, One-Version Rule, error semantics, boundary validation | Designing APIs, module boundaries, or public interfaces |
165:| Skill | What It Does | Use When |
167:| [browser-testing-with-devtools](skills/browser-testing-with-devtools/SKILL.md) | Chrome DevTools MCP for live runtime data - DOM inspection, console logs, network traces, performance profiling | Building or debugging anything that runs in a browser |
168:| [debugging-and-error-recovery](skills/debugging-and-error-recovery/SKILL.md) | Five-step triage: reproduce, localize, reduce, fix, guard. Stop-the-line rule, safe fallbacks | Tests fail, builds break, or behavior is unexpected |
170:### Review - Quality gates before merge
172:| Skill | What It Does | Use When |
174:| [code-review-and-quality](skills/code-review-and-quality/SKILL.md) | Five-axis review, change sizing (~100 lines), severity labels (Nit/Optional/FYI), review speed norms, splitting strategies | Before merging any change |
175:| [code-simplification](skills/code-simplification/SKILL.md) | Chesterton's Fence, Rule of 500, reduce complexity while preserving exact behavior | Code works but is harder to read or maintain than it should be |
176:| [security-and-hardening](skills/security-and-hardening/SKILL.md) | OWASP Top 10 prevention, auth patterns, secrets management, dependency auditing, three-tier boundary system | Handling user input, auth, data storage, or external integrations |
177:| [performance-optimization](skills/performance-optimization/SKILL.md) | Measure-first approach - Core Web Vitals targets, profiling workflows, bundle analysis, anti-pattern detection | Performance requirements exist or you suspect regressions |
179:### Ship - Deploy with confidence
181:| Skill | What It Does | Use When |
183:| [git-workflow-and-versioning](skills/git-workflow-and-versioning/SKILL.md) | Trunk-based development, atomic commits, change sizing (~100 lines), the commit-as-save-point pattern | Making any code change (always) |
184:| [ci-cd-and-automation](skills/ci-cd-and-automation/SKILL.md) | Shift Left, Faster is Safer, feature flags, quality gate pipelines, failure feedback loops | Setting up or modifying build and deploy pipelines |
185:| [deprecation-and-migration](skills/deprecation-and-migration/SKILL.md) | Code-as-liability mindset, compulsory vs advisory deprecation, migration patterns, zombie code removal | Removing old systems, migrating users, or sunsetting features |
186:| [documentation-and-adrs](skills/documentation-and-adrs/SKILL.md) | Architecture Decision Records, API docs, inline documentation standards - document the *why* | Making architectural decisions, changing APIs, or shipping features |
187:| [shipping-and-launch](skills/shipping-and-launch/SKILL.md) | Pre-launch checklists, feature flag lifecycle, staged rollouts, rollback procedures, monitoring setup | Preparing to deploy to production |
191:## Agent Personas
193:Pre-configured specialist personas for targeted reviews:
195:| Agent | Role | Perspective |
197:| [code-reviewer](agents/code-reviewer.md) | Senior Staff Engineer | Five-axis code review with "would a staff engineer approve this?" standard |
198:| [test-engineer](agents/test-engineer.md) | QA Specialist | Test strategy, coverage analysis, and the Prove-It pattern |
199:| [security-auditor](agents/security-auditor.md) | Security Engineer | Vulnerability detection, threat modeling, OWASP assessment |
205:Quick-reference material that skills pull in when needed:
209:| [testing-patterns.md](references/testing-patterns.md) | Test structure, naming, mocking, React/API/E2E examples, anti-patterns |
210:| [security-checklist.md](references/security-checklist.md) | Pre-commit checks, auth, input validation, headers, CORS, OWASP Top 10 |
211:| [performance-checklist.md](references/performance-checklist.md) | Core Web Vitals targets, frontend/backend checklists, measurement commands |
212:| [accessibility-checklist.md](references/accessibility-checklist.md) | Keyboard nav, screen readers, visual design, ARIA, testing tools |
216:## How Skills Work
218:Every skill follows a consistent anatomy:
222:│  SKILL.md                                       │
226:│  │ description: Guides agents through [task].│  │
229:│  Overview         → What this skill does        │
240:- **Process, not prose.** Skills are workflows agents follow, not reference docs they read. Each has steps, checkpoints, and exit criteria.
241:- **Anti-rationalization.** Every skill includes a table of common excuses agents use to skip steps (e.g., "I'll add tests later") with documented counter-arguments.
242:- **Verification is non-negotiable.** Every skill ends with evidence requirements - tests passing, build output, runtime data. "Seems right" is never sufficient.
243:- **Progressive disclosure.** The `SKILL.md` is the entry point. Supporting references load only when needed, keeping token usage minimal.

37:**The performance optimization system for AI agent harnesses. From an Anthropic hackathon winner.**
38:
39:Not just configs. A complete system: skills, instincts, memory optimization, continuous learning, security scanning, and research-first development. Production-ready agents, skills, hooks, rules, MCP configurations, and legacy command shims evolved over 10+ months of intensive daily use building real products.
40:
41:Works across **Claude Code**, **Codex**, **Cursor**, **OpenCode**, **Gemini**, and other AI agent harnesses.
42:
43:ECC v2.0.0-rc.1 adds the public Hermes operator story on top of that reusable layer: start with the [Hermes setup guide](docs/HERMES-SETUP.md), then review the [rc.1 release notes](docs/releases/2.0.0-rc.1/release-notes.md) and [cross-harness architecture](docs/architecture/cross-harness.md).

89:### v2.0.0-rc.1 — Surface Refresh, Operator Workflows, and ECC 2.0 Alpha (Apr 2026)
92:- **Public surface synced to the live repo** — metadata, catalog counts, plugin manifests, and install-facing docs now match the actual OSS surface: 48 agents, 182 skills, and 68 legacy command shims.
95:- **Framework and product surface growth** — `nestjs-patterns`, richer Codex/OpenCode install surfaces, and expanded cross-harness packaging keep the repo usable beyond Claude Code alone.
96:- **ECC 2.0 alpha is in-tree** — the Rust control-plane prototype in `ecc2/` now builds locally and exposes `dashboard`, `start`, `sessions`, `status`, `stop`, `resume`, and `daemon` commands. It is usable as an alpha, not yet a general release.
97:- **Ecosystem hardening** — AgentShield, ECC Tools cost controls, billing portal work, and website refreshes continue to ship around the core plugin instead of drifting into separate silos.
99:### v1.9.0 — Selective Install & Language Expansion (Mar 2026)
101:- **Selective install architecture** — Manifest-driven install pipeline with `install-plan.js` and `install-apply.js` for targeted component installation. State store tracks what's installed and enables incremental updates.
102:- **6 new agents** — `typescript-reviewer`, `pytorch-build-resolver`, `java-build-resolver`, `java-reviewer`, `kotlin-reviewer`, `kotlin-build-resolver` expand language coverage to 10 languages.
103:- **New skills** — `pytorch-patterns` for deep learning workflows, `documentation-lookup` for API reference research, `bun-runtime` and `nextjs-turbopack` for modern JS toolchains, plus 8 operational domain skills and `mcp-server-patterns`.
104:- **Session & state infrastructure** — SQLite state store with query CLI, session adapters for structured recording, skill evolution foundation for self-improving skills.
105:- **Orchestration overhaul** — Harness audit scoring made deterministic, orchestration status and launcher compatibility hardened, observer loop prevention with 5-layer guard.
108:- **Community contributions** — Korean and Chinese translations, biome hook optimization, video processing skills, operational skills, PowerShell installer, Antigravity IDE support.
109:- **CI hardening** — 19 test failure fixes, catalog count enforcement, install manifest validation, and full test suite green.
114:- **Hook reliability overhaul** — SessionStart root fallback, Stop-phase session summaries, and script-based hooks replacing fragile inline one-liners.
115:- **Hook runtime controls** — `ECC_HOOK_PROFILE=minimal|standard|strict` and `ECC_DISABLED_HOOKS=...` for runtime gating without editing hook files.
116:- **New harness commands** — `/harness-audit`, `/loop-start`, `/loop-status`, `/quality-gate`, `/model-route`.

164:See the full changelog in [Releases](https://github.com/affaan-m/everything-claude-code/releases).
174:Most Claude Code users should use exactly one install path:
176:- **Recommended default:** install the Claude Code plugin, then copy only the rule folders you actually want.
177:- **Use the manual installer only if** you want finer-grained control, want to avoid the plugin path entirely, or your Claude Code build has trouble resolving the self-hosted marketplace entry.
178:- **Do not stack install methods.** The most common broken setup is: `/plugin install` first, then `install.sh --profile full` or `npx ecc-install --profile full` afterward.
180:If you already layered multiple installs and things look duplicated, skip straight to [Reset / Uninstall ECC](#reset--uninstall-ecc).
182:### Low-context / no-hooks path
184:If hooks feel too global or you only want ECC's rules, agents, commands, and core workflow skills, skip the plugin and use the minimal manual profile:
187:./install.sh --profile minimal --target claude
191:.\install.ps1 --profile minimal --target claude
193:npx ecc-install --profile minimal --target claude
196:This profile intentionally excludes `hooks-runtime`.
198:If you want the normal core profile but need hooks off, use:
201:./install.sh --profile core --without baseline:hooks --target claude
204:Add hooks later only if you want runtime enforcement:
207:./install.sh --target claude --modules hooks-runtime
212:If you are not sure which ECC profile or component to install, ask the packaged advisor from any project:
218:It returns matching components, related profiles, and preview/install commands. Use the preview command before installing if you want to inspect the exact file plan.
220:### Step 1: Install the Plugin (Recommended)
222:> NOTE: The plugin is convenient, but the OSS installer below is still the most reliable path if your Claude Code build has trouble resolving self-hosted marketplace entries.
225:# Add marketplace
226:/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/affaan-m/everything-claude-code
228:# Install plugin
229:/plugin install everything-claude-code@everything-claude-code
234:ECC now has three public identifiers, and they are not interchangeable:
236:- GitHub source repo: `affaan-m/everything-claude-code`
237:- Claude marketplace/plugin identifier: `everything-claude-code@everything-claude-code`
240:This is intentional. Anthropic marketplace/plugin installs are keyed by a canonical plugin identifier, so ECC standardized on `everything-claude-code@everything-claude-code` to keep the listing name, `/plugin install`, `/plugin list`, and repo docs aligned to one public install surface. Older posts may still show the old short-form nickname; that shorthand is deprecated. Separately, the npm package stayed on `ecc-universal`, so npm installs and marketplace installs intentionally use different names.
242:### Step 2: Install Rules (Required)
244:> WARNING: **Important:** Claude Code plugins cannot distribute `rules` automatically.
246:> If you already installed ECC via `/plugin install`, **do not run `./install.sh --profile full`, `.\install.ps1 --profile full`, or `npx ecc-install --profile full` afterward**. The plugin already loads ECC skills, commands, and hooks. Running the full installer after a plugin install copies those same surfaces into your user directories and can create duplicate skills plus duplicate runtime behavior.
248:> For plugin installs, manually copy only the `rules/` directories you want under `~/.claude/rules/ecc/`. Start with `rules/common` plus one language or framework pack you actually use. Do not copy every rules directory unless you explicitly want all of that context in Claude.
250:> Use the full installer only when you are doing a fully manual ECC install instead of the plugin path.
252:> If your local Claude setup was wiped or reset, that does not mean you need to repurchase ECC. Start with `node scripts/ecc.js list-installed`, then run `node scripts/ecc.js doctor` and `node scripts/ecc.js repair` before reinstalling anything. That usually restores ECC-managed files without rebuilding your setup. If the problem is account or marketplace access for ECC Tools, handle billing/account recovery separately.
256:git clone https://github.com/affaan-m/everything-claude-code.git
257:cd everything-claude-code
259:# Install dependencies (pick your package manager)
260:npm install        # or: pnpm install | yarn install | bun install
262:# Plugin install path: copy only ECC rules into an ECC-owned namespace
267:# Fully manual ECC install path (use this instead of /plugin install)
268:# ./install.sh --profile full
274:# Plugin install path: copy only ECC rules into an ECC-owned namespace
275:New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "$HOME/.claude/rules/ecc" | Out-Null
279:# Fully manual ECC install path (use this instead of /plugin install)
280:# .\install.ps1 --profile full
281:# npx ecc-install --profile full
284:For manual install instructions see the README in the `rules/` folder. When copying rules manually, copy the whole language directory (for example `rules/common` or `rules/golang`), not the files inside it, so relative references keep working and filenames do not collide.
286:### Fully manual install (Fallback)
288:Use this only if you are intentionally skipping the plugin path:
291:./install.sh --profile full
295:.\install.ps1 --profile full
297:npx ecc-install --profile full

--- Z:/repos/deps/anthropics__skills/README.md
1:> **Note:** This repository contains Anthropic's implementation of skills for Claude. For information about the Agent Skills standard, see [agentskills.io](http://agentskills.io).
2:
3:[![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/anthropics/skills)](https://skills.sh/anthropics/skills)
4:
5:# Skills
6:Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically to improve performance on specialized tasks. Skills teach Claude how to complete specific tasks in a repeatable way, whether that's creating documents with your company's brand guidelines, analyzing data using your organization's specific workflows, or automating personal tasks.
7:
8:For more information, check out:
9:- [What are skills?](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512176-what-are-skills)
10:- [Using skills in Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-using-skills-in-claude)
11:- [How to create custom skills](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512198-creating-custom-skills)
12:- [Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills](https://anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills)
13:
14:# About This Repository
15:
16:This repository contains skills that demonstrate what's possible with Claude's skills system. These skills range from creative applications (art, music, design) to technical tasks (testing web apps, MCP server generation) to enterprise workflows (communications, branding, etc.).
17:
18:Each skill is self-contained in its own folder with a `SKILL.md` file containing the instructions and metadata that Claude uses. Browse through these skills to get inspiration for your own skills or to understand different patterns and approaches.
19:
20:Many skills in this repo are open source (Apache 2.0). We've also included the document creation & editing skills that power [Claude's document capabilities](https://www.anthropic.com/news/create-files) under the hood in the [`skills/docx`](./skills/docx), [`skills/pdf`](./skills/pdf), [`skills/pptx`](./skills/pptx), and [`skills/xlsx`](./skills/xlsx) subfolders. These are source-available, not open source, but we wanted to share these with developers as a reference for more complex skills that are actively used in a production AI application.
21:
22:## Disclaimer
23:
24:**These skills are provided for demonstration and educational purposes only.** While some of these capabilities may be available in Claude, the implementations and behaviors you receive from Claude may differ from what is shown in these skills. These skills are meant to illustrate patterns and possibilities. Always test skills thoroughly in your own environment before relying on them for critical tasks.
25:
26:# Skill Sets
27:- [./skills](./skills): Skill examples for Creative & Design, Development & Technical, Enterprise & Communication, and Document Skills
28:- [./spec](./spec): The Agent Skills specification
29:- [./template](./template): Skill template
30:
31:# Try in Claude Code, Claude.ai, and the API
32:
33:## Claude Code
34:You can register this repository as a Claude Code Plugin marketplace by running the following command in Claude Code:
35:```
36:/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills
37:```
38:
39:Then, to install a specific set of skills:
40:1. Select `Browse and install plugins`
41:2. Select `anthropic-agent-skills`
42:3. Select `document-skills` or `example-skills`
43:4. Select `Install now`
44:
45:Alternatively, directly install either Plugin via:
47:/plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills
48:/plugin install example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills
51:After installing the plugin, you can use the skill by just mentioning it. For instance, if you install the `document-skills` plugin from the marketplace, you can ask Claude Code to do something like: "Use the PDF skill to extract the form fields from `path/to/some-file.pdf`"
53:## Claude.ai
55:These example skills are all already available to paid plans in Claude.ai. 
57:To use any skill from this repository or upload custom skills, follow the instructions in [Using skills in Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-using-skills-in-claude#h_a4222fa77b).
59:## Claude API
61:You can use Anthropic's pre-built skills, and upload custom skills, via the Claude API. See the [Skills API Quickstart](https://docs.claude.com/en/api/skills-guide#creating-a-skill) for more.
65:Skills are simple to create - just a folder with a `SKILL.md` file containing YAML frontmatter and instructions. You can use the **template-skill** in this repository as a starting point:
75:[Add your instructions here that Claude will follow when this skill is active]

6:

9:```

12:

14:

16:
17:- Install Claude Code separately: `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`
18:- Specify a custom path: `ClaudeAgentOptions(cli_path="/path/to/claude")`

20:## Quick Start
21:
22:```python
23:import anyio
24:from claude_agent_sdk import query
25:

28:        print(message)
29:
30:anyio.run(main)
31:```

43:        for block in message.content:
44:            if isinstance(block, TextBlock):
45:                print(block.text)

It does not remove tools from Claude's toolset. To block specific tools, use `disallowed_tools`. See the [permissions guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions) for the full evaluation order.

--- Z:/repos/deps/cwc-long-running-agents/README.md
1:# Harness Primitives for Long-Running Claude Agents
2:
3:An agent you can leave running for hours needs more than a good prompt. It needs a small amount of structure around it: enforcement that "done" means observed evidence, an independent check on its own claims, and a way for the next session to pick up cleanly where this one left off. [Effective Harnesses for Long-Running Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents) (Nov 2025) and [Harness Design for Long-Running Application Development](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps) (Mar 2026) describe these patterns; this repo is the code companion. It ships a short, readable example of each as a native [Claude Code hook](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) or subagent, so you can see the mechanism, copy what fits, and wire it into your own harness.
4:
5:Three primitives form the quality loop:
6:
7:- **Default-FAIL contract.** Every criterion starts `false`; the agent can't mark it passing without opening evidence first.
8:- **Fresh-context evaluator.** A separate agent with no Write/Edit tools grades the work from a context window that never saw the build.
9:- **Agent-maintained handoff.** The agent writes its own progress notes and commits to git so the next session picks up cleanly.
10:
11:Two more operator-control hooks are included for when you want to watch or intervene. The same patterns translate directly to `PreToolUse`/`Stop` callbacks in the [Agent SDK](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/sdk).
12:
13:> Built as the take-home for the Long-Running Agents station at Code with Claude 2026. **These are example ingredients, not a turnkey harness.** Event demo; not maintained and not accepting contributions.
14:
15:## How to use this repo
16:
17:**Read and cherry-pick.** Each primitive is one standalone file with no dependency on the others. The [quality-loop table](#the-quality-loop) below maps every one to its example here and its Agent SDK equivalent. Open the file, see how the mechanism works, copy what fits.
18:
19:**Or copy all of them as a starting point.** In your project, run `claude` and paste:
20:
21:> Clone github.com/anthropics/cwc-long-running-agents into /tmp, copy its `claude-code-config/.claude/` directory into this project's root, make the hook scripts executable, then walk me through what each hook and the evaluator subagent does and what I'll need to adapt for this project.
22:
23:or do it yourself:
24:
25:```bash
26:cp -r claude-code-config/.claude /path/to/your/project/
27:chmod +x /path/to/your/project/.claude/hooks/*.sh
28:```
29:
30:Either way, this gives you all the examples wired into `.claude/` at once. Before relying on them: point `RESULTS_FILE` at your project's actual results file, adjust the evidence-file pattern in `track-read.sh`, and run `claude` from the directory that contains `.claude/` (hooks are not loaded when launching from a subdirectory).
31:
32:**If you're on the Agent SDK,** this repo is a pattern reference. The shell hooks here translate one-to-one to `PreToolUse`/`Stop` callbacks. To scaffold an SDK agent from inside Claude Code, install the [`agent-sdk-dev` plugin](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/plugins/agent-sdk-dev) and ask Claude to build an agent that implements whichever of these primitives you want. For a hand-written starting point, see the [autonomous-coding quickstart](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts/tree/main/autonomous-coding) or the [agent-sdk-workshop](https://github.com/anthropics/agent-sdk-workshop) curriculum.
33:
34:## The quality loop
35:
36:| Primitive | Claude Code example | Agent SDK equivalent | Enforcement |
37:|---|---|---|---|
38:| **Default-FAIL contract** | [`hooks/track-read.sh`](./claude-code-config/.claude/hooks/track-read.sh) + [`hooks/verify-gate.sh`](./claude-code-config/.claude/hooks/verify-gate.sh) | `PreToolUse` callback | hook |
39:| **Fresh-context evaluator** | [`agents/evaluator.md`](./claude-code-config/.claude/agents/evaluator.md) subagent (no Write/Edit) | [`evaluator_optimizer.ipynb`](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/blob/main/patterns/agents/evaluator_optimizer.ipynb) | you invoke it |
40:| **Agent-maintained handoff** | [`CLAUDE.md`](./claude-code-config/.claude/CLAUDE.md) + [`hooks/commit-on-stop.sh`](./claude-code-config/.claude/hooks/commit-on-stop.sh) | system prompt + `Stop` callback | convention + hook backstop |
41:
42:### Default-FAIL contract
43:
44:Agents will mark a feature "passing" after a unit test or a curl when the UI is visibly broken. Asking nicely in the prompt doesn't reliably stop this. The harness makes "done" structural. Every feature is a row in a `test-results.json` file you create in your project:
45:
50:The only evidence that counts is a file matching the patterns in `track-read.sh` (screenshots, console logs, result files), and a `PreToolUse` hook denies any write to the results file unless the agent has first opened one with the Read tool. The agent can't claim success it hasn't observed. (The shipped hook is intentionally simple; see the comments in `verify-gate.sh` for the gaps a production version would close.)
54:The builder shouldn't grade its own work. After each feature, you (or your wrapper script) invoke a separate subagent (`agents/evaluator.md`) with no Write/Edit tools that reviews the diff and the screenshots from a context window that never saw the build, then returns `PASS` or `NEEDS_WORK` with specific findings. On `NEEDS_WORK` the findings become the next builder session's starting prompt, closing the build/evaluate/rebuild loop. Invoke it from your wrapper with `claude --agent evaluator -p "<review prompt>"`; what your loop does with the verdict is up to you.
58:A fresh session has no memory of what the previous one did, and when a long session fills its context window Claude Code summarizes the history, which loses detail. So the agent maintains the handoff itself: it scopes each session to one feature, writes to a structured `PROGRESS.md` as it works and re-reads it first thing on every restart, and `git add`s and commits at meaningful checkpoints so `git log` is a second record. `commit-on-stop.sh` is the backstop that catches whatever's still uncommitted at session end. This is the layer most sensitive to model capability; newer models drift less and self-scope better, so re-evaluate how much of `CLAUDE.md` you still need after each model release (see [Re-simplify on model upgrades](#going-further)).
64:Two more hooks for when you want to watch the loop run or intervene mid-stream. These aren't part of the quality story; they're how a human stays in the loop.
68:| [`hooks/kill-switch.sh`](./claude-code-config/.claude/hooks/kill-switch.sh) | Halts every tool call while an `AGENT_STOP` file exists at the project root. |
69:| [`hooks/steer.sh`](./claude-code-config/.claude/hooks/steer.sh) | Surfaces the contents of `STEER.md` (project root) to the agent once and clears it, so you can redirect mid-run without restarting. |
79:watch -n 2 'wc -l < .claude/.evidence-reads 2>/dev/null'   # evidence reads (resets to 0 after each gated write)
82:Run them in a `tmux` grid and you have a live view of every primitive.
90:| **Unattended loop** | Cap session length and have an outer script start the next one (pick next feature, build, evaluate, reset) | [Why naive implementations fall short](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps#why-naive-implementations-fall-short); [`ralph-loop`](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/plugins/ralph-loop) plugin |
93:| **Grading rubrics** | Give the evaluator scoring principles (functionality, design, craft, originality) with few-shot examples instead of binary pass/fail | [Frontend design: making subjective quality gradable](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps#frontend-design-making-subjective-quality-gradable); [`frontend-design`](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/plugins/frontend-design) plugin |
94:| **Browser-verified evaluator** | Let the evaluator open the running app itself instead of trusting the builder's screenshots | [Frontend design](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps#frontend-design-making-subjective-quality-gradable) (Playwright MCP usage); add [`@playwright/mcp`](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp) or Claude in Chrome to `tools:` in `agents/evaluator.md` |
95:| **Re-simplify on model upgrades** | After each model release, comment out harness pieces one at a time and see what's still load-bearing | [What comes next](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps#what-comes-next); [Harnessing Claude's Intelligence](https://claude.com/blog/harnessing-claudes-intelligence) |
96:| **Hosted runtime** | Anthropic hosts the loop, sandbox, and scheduling so you don't run any of this yourself | [Claude Managed Agents](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/managed-agents) |
101:claude --agent evaluator -p "Review the diff and screenshots/ for feature N against its spec."

210:| use recaps for long-running sessions — short summaries of what Claude did and what's next, useful when returning after minutes or hours. Disable with recaps in /config | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](tips/claude-boris-6-tips-16-apr-26.md) |

[60 lines in humanlayer](https://www.humanlayer.dev/blog/writing-a-good-claude-md) ([still not 100% guaranteed](https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeCode/comments/1qn9pb9/claudemd_says_must_use_agent_claude_ignores_it_80/)) | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2007179840848597422) [![Dex](!/tags/community-dex.svg)](https://www.humanlayer.dev/blog/writing-a-good-claude-md) |
220:| use [multiple CLAUDE.md](best-practice/claude-memory.md) for monorepos — ancestor + descendant loading | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2016339448863355206) |
222:| any developer should be able to launch Claude, say "run the tests" and it works on the first try — if it doesn't, your CLAUDE.md is missing essential setup/build/test commands | [![Dex](!/tags/community-dex.svg)](https://x.com/dexhorthy/status/2034713765401551053) |
223:| keep codebases clean and finish migrations — partially migrated frameworks confuse models that might pick the wrong pattern | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://youtu.be/julbw1JuAz0?t=1112) [![Video](!/tags/video.svg)](https://youtu.be/julbw1JuAz0?t=1112) |
224:| use [settings.json](best-practice/claude-settings.md) for harness-enforced behavior (attribution, permissions, model) — don't put "NEVER add Co-Authored-By" in CLAUDE.md when attribution.commit: "" is deterministic | [![davila7](!/tags/community-davila7.svg)](https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2036182734310195550) |
226:<a id="tips-agents"></a><img src="!/tags/a.svg" height="14"> **Agents (4)**
230:| have feature specific [sub-agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) (extra context) with [skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) (progressive disclosure) instead of general qa, backend engineer | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2007179850139000872) |
231:| say "use subagents" to throw more compute at a problem — offload tasks to keep your main context clean and focused 🚫👶 | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2017742755737555434) |
232:| [agent teams with tmux](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams) and [git worktrees](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2025007393290272904) for parallel development | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2025007393290272904) |
233:| use [test time compute](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) — separate context windows make results better; one agent can cause bugs and another (same model) can find them | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2031151689219321886) |
235:<a id="tips-commands"></a><img src="!/tags/c.svg" height="14"> **Commands (3)**
239:| use [commands](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slash-commands) for your workflows instead of [sub-agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2007179847949500714) |
240:| use [slash commands](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slash-commands) for every "inner loop" workflow you do many times a day — saves repeated prompting, commands live in .claude/commands/ and are checked into git | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2007179847949500714) |
241:| if you do something more than once a day, turn it into a [skill](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) or [command](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slash-commands) — build /techdebt, context-dump, or analytics commands | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2017742748984742078) |
243:<a id="tips-skills"></a><img src="!/tags/s.svg" height="14"> **Skills (9)**
247:| use [context: fork](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) to run a skill in an isolated subagent — main context only sees the final result, not intermediate tool calls. The agent field lets you set the subagent type | [![Lydia](!/tags/lydia.svg)](https://x.com/lydiahallie/status/2033603164398883042) |
248:| use [skills in subfolders](reports/claude-skills-for-larger-mono-repos.md) for monorepos | [![Claude](!/tags/claude.svg)](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) |
249:| skills are folders, not files — use references/, scripts/, examples/ subdirectories for [progressive disclosure](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) | [![Thariq](!/tags/thariq.svg)](https://x.com/trq212/status/2033949937936085378) |
252:| don't state the obvious in skills — focus on what pushes Claude out of its default behavior 🚫👶 | [![Thariq](!/tags/thariq.svg)](https://x.com/trq212/status/2033949937936085378) |
253:| don't railroad Claude in skills — give goals and constraints, not prescriptive step-by-step instructions 🚫👶 | [![Thariq](!/tags/thariq.svg)](https://x.com/trq212/status/2033949937936085378) |
254:| include scripts and libraries in skills so Claude composes rather than reconstructs boilerplate | [![Thariq](!/tags/thariq.svg)](https://x.com/trq212/status/2033949937936085378) |
261:| use [on-demand hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) in skills — /careful blocks destructive commands, /freeze blocks edits outside a directory | [![Thariq](!/tags/thariq.svg)](https://x.com/trq212/status/2033949937936085378) |
262:| [measure skill usage](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) with a PreToolUse hook to find popular or undertriggering skills | [![Thariq](!/tags/thariq.svg)](https://x.com/trq212/status/2033949937936085378) |
263:| use a [PostToolUse hook](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) to auto-format code — Claude generates well-formatted code, the hook handles the last 10% to avoid CI failures | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2007179852047335529) |
264:| route [permission requests](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) to Opus via a hook — let it scan for attacks and auto-approve safe ones 🚫👶 | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2017742755737555434) |
265:| use a [Stop hook](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) to nudge Claude to keep going or verify its work at the end of a turn | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2021701059253874861) |
271:| use [/model](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config) to select model and reasoning, [/context](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode) to see context usage, [/usage](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs) to check plan limits, [/extra-usage](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode) to configure overflow billing, [/config](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings) to configure settings — use Opus for plan mode and Sonnet for code to get the best of both | [![Cat](!/tags/cat-wu.svg)](https://x.com/_catwu/status/1955694117264261609) |
272:| always use [thinking mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config) true (to see reasoning) and [Output Style](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/output-styles) Explanatory (to see detailed output with ★ Insight boxes) in [/config](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings) for better understanding of Claude's decisions | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2007179838864666847) |
274:| /focus mode hides all intermediate work and shows only the final result — trust the model to run the right commands and just look at the outcome (toggle with /focus) | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](tips/claude-boris-6-tips-16-apr-26.md) |
275:| tune effort level with Opus 4.7's adaptive thinking — low for speed and fewer tokens, max for most intelligence (slider: low · medium · high · xhigh · max) | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](tips/claude-boris-6-tips-16-apr-26.md) |
281:| use ASCII diagrams a lot to understand your architecture | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2017742759218794768) |
282:| use [/loop](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks) for local recurring monitoring (up to 7 days) · use [/schedule](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines) for cloud-based recurring tasks that run even when your machine is off | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2038454341884154269) |
283:| use [Ralph Wiggum plugin](https://github.com/shanraisshan/ralph-wiggum-self-evolving-loop) for long-running autonomous tasks | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2007179858435281082) |
284:| [/permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions) with wildcard syntax (Bash(npm run *), Edit(/docs/**)) instead of dangerously-skip-permissions | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2007179854077407667) |
285:| [/sandbox](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing) to reduce permission prompts with file and network isolation — 84% reduction internally | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2021700506465579443) [![Cat](!/tags/cat-wu.svg)](https://creatoreconomy.so/p/inside-claude-code-how-an-ai-native-actually-works-cat-wu) |
286:| invest in [product verification](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) skills (signup-flow-driver, checkout-verifier) — worth spending a week to perfect | [![Thariq](!/tags/thariq.svg)](https://x.com/trq212/status/2033949937936085378) |
287:| use [auto mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode) instead of dangerously-skip-permissions — a model-based classifier decides if each command is safe and auto-approves, pauses and asks if risky. Shift+Tab to cycle Ask → Plan → Auto modes 🚫👶 | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](tips/claude-boris-6-tips-16-apr-26.md) |
288:| use /less-permission-prompts skill to scan session history for safe bash/MCP commands that repeatedly prompt, then get a recommended allowlist to paste into [settings](best-practice/claude-settings.md) | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](tips/claude-boris-6-tips-16-apr-26.md) |
289:| build a /go skill that (1) tests end-to-end via bash/browser/computer use (2) runs /simplify (3) puts up a PR — so when you come back, you know the code works 🚫👶 | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](tips/claude-boris-6-tips-16-apr-26.md) |
295:| keep PRs small and focused — [p50 of 118 lines](tips/claude-boris-2-tips-25-mar-26.md) (141 PRs, 45K lines changed in a day), one feature per PR, easier to review and revert | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2038552880018538749) |
296:| always [squash merge](tips/claude-boris-2-tips-25-mar-26.md) PRs — clean linear history, one commit per feature, easy git revert and git bisect | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2038552880018538749) |
297:| commit often — try to commit at least once per hour, as soon as task is completed, commit | ![Shayan](!/tags/community-shayan.svg) |
298:| tag [@claude](https://github.com/apps/claude) on a coworker's PR to auto-generate lint rules for recurring review feedback — automate yourself out of code review 🚫👶 | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://youtu.be/julbw1JuAz0?t=2715) [![Video](!/tags/video.svg)](https://youtu.be/julbw1JuAz0?t=2715) |
299:| use [/code-review](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review) for multi-agent PR analysis — catches bugs, security vulnerabilities, and regressions before merge | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2031089411820228645) |
310:| agentic search (glob + grep) beats RAG — Claude Code tried and discarded vector databases because code drifts out of sync and permissions are complex | [![Boris](!/tags/boris-cherny.svg)](https://youtu.be/julbw1JuAz0?t=3095) [![Video](!/tags/video.svg)](https://youtu.be/julbw1JuAz0?t=3095) |

1:# Sub-agents Best Practice
2:
3:![Last Updated](https://img.shields.io/badge/Last_Updated-May%2001%2C%202026%203%3A30%20PM%20PKT-white?style=flat&labelColor=555) ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude_Code-v2.1.126-blue?style=flat&labelColor=555)<br>
4:[![Implemented](https://img.shields.io/badge/Implemented-2ea44f?style=flat)](../implementation/claude-subagents-implementation.md)
5:
6:Claude Code subagents — frontmatter fields and official built-in agent types.
7:
8:<table width="100%">
9:<tr>
10:<td><a href="../">← Back to Claude Code Best Practice</a></td>
11:<td align="right"><img src="../!/claude-jumping.svg" alt="Claude" width="60" /></td>
12:</tr>

16:
17:## Frontmatter Fields (16)
18:
19:| Field | Type | Required | Description |
20:|-------|------|----------|-------------|
21:| `name` | string | Yes | Unique identifier using lowercase letters and hyphens |
22:| `description` | string | Yes | When to invoke. Use `"PROACTIVELY"` for auto-invocation by Claude |
23:| `tools` | string/list | No | Comma-separated allowlist of tools (e.g., `Read, Write, Edit, Bash`). Inherits all tools if omitted. Supports `Agent(agent_type)` syntax to restrict spawnable subagents; the older `Task(agent_type)` alias still works |
24:| `disallowedTools` | string/list | No | Tools to deny, removed from inherited or specified list |
25:| `model` | string | No | Model to use: `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, a full model ID (e.g., `claude-opus-4-6`), or `inherit` (default: `inherit`) |
26:| `permissionMode` | string | No | Permission mode: `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, or `plan` |
27:| `maxTurns` | integer | No | Maximum number of agentic turns before the subagent stops |
28:| `skills` | list | No | Skill names to preload into agent context at startup (full content injected, not just made available) |
29:| `mcpServers` | list | No | MCP servers for this subagent — server name strings or inline `{name: config}` objects |
30:| `hooks` | object | No | Lifecycle hooks scoped to this subagent. All hook events are supported; `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, and `Stop` are the most common |
31:| `memory` | string | No | Persistent memory scope: `user`, `project`, or `local` |
32:| `background` | boolean | No | Set to `true` to always run as a background task (default: `false`) |
33:| `effort` | string | No | Effort level override when this subagent is active: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` (Opus 4.6 only). Default: inherits from session |
34:| `isolation` | string | No | Set to `"worktree"` to run in a temporary git worktree (auto-cleaned if no changes) |
35:| `initialPrompt` | string | No | Auto-submitted as the first user turn when this agent runs as the main session agent (via `--agent` or the `agent` setting). Commands and skills are processed. Prepended to any user-provided prompt |
36:| `color` | string | No | Display color for the subagent in the task list and transcript: `red`, `blue`, `green`, `yellow`, `purple`, `orange`, `pink`, or `cyan` |
37:
38:---
39:
40:## ![Official](../!/tags/official.svg) **(5)**
41:
42:| # | Agent | Model | Tools | Description |
43:|---|-------|-------|-------|-------------|
44:| 1 | `general-purpose` | inherit | All | Complex multi-step tasks — the default agent type for research, code search, and autonomous work |
45:| 2 | `Explore` | haiku | Read-only (no Write, Edit) | Fast codebase search and exploration — optimized for finding files, searching code, and answering codebase questions |
46:| 3 | `Plan` | inherit | Read-only (no Write, Edit) | Pre-planning research in plan mode — explores the codebase and designs implementation approaches before writing code |
47:| 4 | `statusline-setup` | sonnet | Read, Edit | Configures the user's Claude Code status line setting |
48:| 5 | `claude-code-guide` | haiku | Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch | Answers questions about Claude Code features, Agent SDK, and Claude API |

32:## Settings Hierarchy
33:
34:Settings apply in order of precedence (highest to lowest):
35:
36:| Priority | Location | Scope | Shared? | Purpose |
37:|----------|----------|-------|---------|---------|
38:| 1 | Managed settings | Organization | Yes (deployed by IT) | Security policies that cannot be overridden |
39:| 2 | Command line arguments | Session | N/A | Temporary single-session overrides |
40:| 3 | `.claude/settings.local.json` | Project | No (git-ignored) | Personal project-specific |
41:| 4 | `.claude/settings.json` | Project | Yes (committed) | Team-shared settings |
42:| 5 | `~/.claude/settings.json` | User | N/A | Global personal defaults |
43:
44:**Managed settings** are organization-enforced and cannot be overridden by any other level, including command line arguments. Delivery methods:
45:- **Server-managed** settings (remote delivery)
46:- **MDM profiles** — macOS plist at `com.anthropic.claudecode`
47:- **Registry policies** — Windows `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode` (admin) and `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode` (user-level, lowest policy priority)
48:- **File** — `managed-settings.json` and `managed-mcp.json` (macOS: `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/`, Linux/WSL: `/etc/claude-code/`, Windows: `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\`)
49:- **Drop-in directory** — `managed-settings.d/` alongside `managed-settings.json` for independent policy fragments (v2.1.83). Following the systemd convention, `managed-settings.json` is merged first as the base, then all `*.json` files in the drop-in directory are sorted alphabetically and merged on top. Later files override earlier ones for scalar values; arrays are concatenated and de-duplicated; objects are deep-merged. Hidden files starting with `.` are ignored. Use numeric prefixes to control merge order (e.g., `10-telemetry.json`, `20-security.json`)
50:
51:Within the managed tier, precedence is: server-managed > MDM/OS-level policies > file-based (`managed-settings.d/*.json` + `managed-settings.json`) > HKCU registry (Windows only). Only one managed source is used; sources do not merge across tiers. Within the file-based tier, drop-in files and the base file are merged together.
52:
53:> **Note:** As of v2.1.75, the deprecated Windows fallback path `C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json` has been removed. Use `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json` instead.
54:
55:> **Note (v2.1.126):** `/config` now persists changes to `~/.claude/settings.json` instead of holding them in memory only. Edits made through the interactive Config UI survive restarts.
59:- Managed settings may lock or override local behavior even if local files specify different values.
60:- Array settings (e.g., `permissions.allow`) are **concatenated and deduplicated** across scopes — entries from all levels are combined, not replaced.
66:### General Settings
70:| `$schema` | string | - | JSON Schema URL for IDE validation and autocompletion (e.g., `"https://json.schemastore.org/claude-code-settings.json"`) |
72:| `agent` | string | - | Set the default agent for the main conversation. Value is the agent name from `.claude/agents/`. Also available via `--agent` CLI flag |
74:| `cleanupPeriodDays` | number | `30` | Age cutoff for the startup cleanup sweep (minimum 1). Inactive session transcripts and orphaned subagent worktrees are deleted; as of v2.1.117 the sweep also covers `~/.claude/tasks/`, `~/.claude/shell-snapshots/`, and `~/.claude/backups/`. Setting to `0` is rejected with a validation error. To disable transcript writes in non-interactive mode (`-p`), use `--no-session-persistence` or `persistSession: false` SDK option |
78:| `skipWebFetchPreflight` | boolean | `false` | Skip WebFetch blocklist check before fetching URLs *(in JSON schema, not on official settings page)* |
81:| `defaultShell` | string | `"bash"` | Default shell for input-box `!` commands. Accepts `"bash"` (default) or `"powershell"`. Setting `"powershell"` routes interactive `!` commands through PowerShell on Windows. Requires `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1` (v2.1.84). **v2.1.120:** When PowerShell is available, it is used as the fallback shell on Windows even without Git for Windows installed. **v2.1.126:** When PowerShell is enabled, it is treated as the *primary* shell instead of defaulting to Bash. PowerShell 7 detection now also covers Microsoft Store installs, MSI installs not on PATH, and `.NET` global tool installs |
82:| `includeGitInstructions` | boolean | `true` | Include built-in commit and PR workflow instructions and the git status snapshot in Claude's system prompt. The `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS` environment variable takes precedence over this setting when set |
83:| `voice` | object | - | Voice dictation configuration. Object with three fields: `enabled` (boolean — push-to-talk on/off), `mode` (string — `"hold"` for hold-to-talk or `"tap"` for tap-to-toggle), and `autoSubmit` (boolean — submit transcript immediately when dictation ends). Written automatically when you run `/voice`. Requires a Claude.ai account (v2.1.118 expanded structure) |
84:| `voiceEnabled` | boolean | - | **DEPRECATED** — legacy alias for `voice.enabled`. Use the `voice` object instead to get `mode` and `autoSubmit` controls |
87:| `disableDeepLinkRegistration` | string | - | Set to `"disable"` to prevent Claude Code from registering the `claude-cli://` protocol handler with the operating system on startup. Deep links let external tools open a Claude Code session with a pre-filled prompt via `claude-cli://open?q=...`. The `q` parameter supports multi-line prompts using URL-encoded newlines (`%0A`). Useful in environments where protocol handler registration is restricted or managed separately |
89:| `disableSkillShellExecution` | boolean | `false` | Disable inline shell execution for `` !`...` `` and `` ```! `` blocks in skills and custom commands from user, project, plugin, or additional-directory sources. Commands are replaced with `[shell command execution disabled by policy]` instead of being run. Bundled and managed skills are not affected (v2.1.91) |
90:| `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` | boolean | `false` | **(Managed only)** Block CLI startup until remote managed settings are freshly fetched. If the fetch fails, the CLI exits (fail-closed). Use in enterprise environments where policy enforcement must be up-to-date before any session begins (v2.1.92) |
91:| `wslInheritsWindowsSettings` | boolean | `false` | **(Windows managed settings only)** When `true`, Claude Code on WSL reads managed settings from the Windows policy chain (HKLM registry + `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json`) in addition to `/etc/claude-code`, with Windows sources taking priority. Only honored when set in the HKLM registry key or `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json`, both of which require Windows admin to write. For HKCU policy to also apply on WSL, the flag must additionally be set in HKCU itself. Has no effect on native Windows (v2.1.118) |
115:| `autoMemoryDirectory` | string | - | Custom directory for auto-memory storage. Accepts `~/`-expanded paths. Not accepted in project settings (`.claude/settings.json`) to prevent redirecting memory writes to sensitive locations; accepted from policy, local, and user settings |
